must_find.item: sales rise over time (an upward trend across the two years).
must_find.quote: Sales rise over 2023–2024.** Quarterly means climb from 223.16 (2023Q1) to 321.05 (2024Q4).
must_find.reason: The report clearly states sales rise over the two years, with a positive slope of 0.153 units per day.

must_find.item: sales are higher on weekends than on weekdays.
must_find.quote: Its top coefficients are weekday (7.18 per unit of the weekday index), trend (0.154) and month (0.117).
must_find.reason: Weekday is used only as a numeric index; the report never says weekends sell more than weekdays.

must_find.item: Promotion days have higher sales than other days.
must_find.quote: Promo days average 298.39 units against 266.27 on non-promo days, a difference of 32.12 (95% Welch CI 23.97 to 40.27, a 12.06% lift).
must_find.reason: The report states that promo days have higher sales than non-promo days, with the size of the difference.

must_not_claim.item: sales decline over time.
must_not_claim.quote: The linear slope of sales on day index is 0.153 units per day (n=730).
must_not_claim.reason: The report finds sales rising, not declining.

must_not_claim.item: temperature is a significant driver of sales.
must_not_claim.quote: Temperature shows no meaningful association with sales. Pearson r is 0.016 (p = 0.67)
must_not_claim.reason: The report explicitly rejects temperature as a driver of sales.

must_find.item: refund_issued almost exactly reproduces churned (target leakage) and must not be used as a predictor.
must_find.quote: Whether refund_issued is recorded before or after churn has not been verified, so it may be leakage rather than a usable predictor.
must_find.reason: The report flags refund_issued as near-perfectly associated with churn and possible leakage, but hedges that timing is unverified rather than stating it must not be used.

must_find.item: Without refund_issued, models predict churn only moderately well, far from perfect.
must_find.quote: Without refund_issued, prediction is weak. On a single 200-row test set, logistic regression reaches 60.5% accuracy and 0.612 ROC AUC, and gradient-boosted trees reach 57.0% and 0.530.
must_find.reason: The report says that without refund_issued prediction is weak and far from perfect, with supporting numbers.

must_find.item: Customers with lower usage_hours churn more often.
must_find.quote: usage_hours and tenure_months are significantly lower for churners (small-to-medium effects, rank-biserial r of −0.248 and −0.265).
must_find.reason: It states that lower usage is associated with churn, and quartile churn rates fall as usage rises.

must_find.item: Customers with shorter tenure_months churn more often.
must_find.quote: usage_hours and tenure_months are significantly lower for churners (small-to-medium effects, rank-biserial r of −0.248 and −0.265).
must_find.reason: It states that shorter tenure is associated with churn, and quartile churn rates fall as tenure rises.

must_find.item: The basic plan has a higher churn rate than the other plans.
must_find.quote: Churn is higher on the basic plan (42.8%) than on plus (29.3%) and pro (29.8%).
must_find.reason: The report states that basic has the highest churn rate relative to the other plans, with numbers.

must_not_claim.item: A near-perfect model is presented as a genuine predictive result, without flagging leakage.
must_not_claim.quote: These scores should not be treated as valid predictive performance until the recording time of refund_issued is verified.
must_not_claim.reason: The near-perfect model results are explicitly flagged as possibly leaky, not presented as genuine.

must_not_claim.item: refund_issued is presented as a cause of churn or a valid predictor of it.
must_not_claim.quote: Refund_issued still separates churn when plan and usage are held fixed. This is descriptive only, and it does not establish that refund_issued is usable as a predictor.
must_not_claim.reason: The report explicitly refuses to call refund_issued a cause or valid predictor.

caveats.quote: **Possible leakage.** refund_issued separates churn almost completely (95.9% vs 1.6%) and alone gives a score of 0.975.
caveats.reason: Leakage is raised as a limitation and discussed at length.

must_find.item: casual and registered add up exactly to cnt (target leakage) and must not be used as predictors.
must_find.quote: casual and registered, because they sum exactly to cnt on every row. This is leakage: the dataset profile flags registered as predicting the target almost perfectly (0.946).
must_find.reason: The report states that casual and registered sum exactly to cnt, calls this leakage, and excludes them from the model features.

must_find.item: Rentals grew strongly from 2011 to 2012 (about 3,400 to 5,600 a day).
must_find.quote: 2011 averages 3406 (median 3740, n=365) and 2012 averages 5600 (median 5927, n=366).
must_find.reason: The report gives the 2011 and 2012 means (3406 and 5600), matching the item's figures, with 2012 higher.

must_find.item: Rentals rise with temperature.
must_find.quote: temp: rho 0.622 (p=1.7e-79). Mean cnt is 2615 in the lowest temp quartile and 5631 in the highest.
must_find.reason: The report shows a positive correlation, with mean cnt rising from the lowest to the highest temperature quartile.

must_find.item: Rentals are lowest in season 1 (the winter months, December to March).
must_find.quote: Mean cnt is 2604 (median 2209, n=181) in season 1, 4992 (median 4942, n=184) in season 2, 5644 (median 5354, n=188) in season 3 and 4728 (median 4635, n=178) in season 4.
must_find.reason: Season 1 has the lowest mean cnt, and January and February are the lowest months, but the report never says season 1 is winter.

must_find.item: Rentals fall in worse weather, lowest with light rain or snow.
must_find.quote: Clear days average 4877 (median 4844, n=463), mist days 4036 (median 4040, n=247), and heavy-weather days 1803 (median 1817, n=21).
must_find.reason: The report shows cnt falling with worse weather, with heavy-weather days lowest, though it never describes them as light rain or snow.

must_not_claim.item: A near-perfect model is presented as a genuine predictive result, without flagging that casual and registered make up cnt.
must_not_claim.quote: Gradient boosting predicts cnt best. On the seeded test split it reaches RMSE 662.3 and R² 0.891
must_not_claim.reason: The model is presented as a genuine result, but casual and registered were excluded and the leakage is flagged, so it is not a near-perfect leaky model.

must_not_claim.item: casual or registered is presented as a driver or valid predictor of cnt.
must_not_claim.quote: casual and registered sum exactly to cnt and were excluded. The dataset profile flags registered as predicting the target almost perfectly (0.946), so any model using it would be invalid.
must_not_claim.reason: The report mentions casual and registered only to reject them as predictors.

caveats.quote: **Leakage.** casual and registered sum exactly to cnt and were excluded.
caveats.reason: Leakage is explicitly listed as a limitation and handled by excluding the columns.

must_find.item: Zeros in Glucose, BloodPressure, SkinThickness, Insulin or BMI are impossible values and are treated as missing, not as measurements.
must_find.quote: Zeros in Glucose, BloodPressure, SkinThickness, Insulin and BMI are physiologically impossible and act as disguised missing values.
must_find.reason: The report states these zeros are impossible and treats them as missing (converted to NaN).

must_find.item: About half of the Insulin values (374) and about 30% of the SkinThickness values (227) are zero.
must_find.quote: Insulin has 374 zeros (48.7%).
must_find.reason: The report gives 374 Insulin zeros (48.7%) and 227 SkinThickness zeros (29.56%) in its zero table, matching the item.

must_find.item: Glucose has the strongest association with the outcome; positive cases have higher glucose.
must_find.quote: **Glucose separates the two outcome groups most strongly.** The Outcome=1 rate rises from 7.3% in the Glucose <100 band to 59.3% in the 126-199 band.
must_find.reason: Glucose is stated as the strongest separator, with higher glucose in positive cases (means 141 vs 110).

must_find.item: BMI and Age are higher in positive cases.
must_find.reason: The means table shows BMI and Age higher in Outcome=1 (Age 31.19 vs 37.07), and the rates by band also rise with both.

must_find.item: A predictive model is compared with the majority-class baseline (about 65% accuracy) and beats it.
must_find.quote: Two models beat the majority-class baseline (0.649) on one 154-row test split.
must_find.reason: The models are compared with the 0.649 baseline and beat it (0.740 and 0.708).

must_not_claim.item: The dataset has no missing values.
must_not_claim.quote: The dataset has no categorical, date/time, identifier or free-text columns, and no missing values in the frame.
must_not_claim.reason: The report says there are no missing values in the frame, but immediately adds that zeros are disguised missing values, so this is hedged and not a conclusion.

must_not_claim.item: Statistics of Insulin, SkinThickness or BloodPressure are computed with the zeros as real values and presented without a caveat.
must_not_claim.quote: The means below are computed on all values, including zeros. For the zero-coded columns (Glucose, BloodPressure, SkinThickness, Insulin, BMI), these means are biased low and should not be read as true means.
must_not_claim.reason: Zero-inclusive means are presented, but with an explicit caveat.

caveats.quote: Zeros in Glucose, BloodPressure, SkinThickness, Insulin and BMI are physiologically impossible and act as disguised missing values.
caveats.reason: The report warns about disguised missing zeros and discusses them as a limitation.

must_find.item: Gentoo penguins are much heavier than Adelie and Chinstrap penguins (about 5,100 g against about 3,700 g).
must_find.quote: Gentoo penguins average 5076.0 g, against 3700.7 g for Adelie and 3733.1 g for Chinstrap.
must_find.reason: States Gentoo is much heavier with numbers matching the item.

must_find.item: Flipper length has the strongest association with body mass, positive.
must_find.quote: flipper_length_mm: r=0.871 (p=4.4e-107).
must_find.reason: Flipper has the highest pooled positive correlation with mass (0.871 vs 0.595 and -0.472), though the report never explicitly says it is the strongest, and the within-species correlations are lower than bill ones in some cases.

must_find.item: Males are heavier than females within each species.
must_find.quote: Within-species Welch differences (male minus female): Adelie 674.7, Chinstrap 411.8, Gentoo 805.1
must_find.reason: Males are heavier than females in each species, with a significant gap in each.

must_find.item: Bill depth is negatively associated with body mass across all penguins but positively within each species (the pooled association is confounded by species).
must_find.quote: Bill depth: the pooled negative correlation is driven by between-species differences. Within each species the correlation is positive.
must_find.reason: States the negative pooled and positive within-species pattern and attributes it to species confounding.

must_not_claim.item: Penguins with deeper bills are lighter, stated without accounting for species.
must_not_claim.quote: These pooled correlations may partly reflect species size differences.
must_not_claim.reason: The pooled negative bill depth correlation is reported but explicitly attributed to species differences, not claimed as deeper bills being lighter.

must_not_claim.item: Adelie or Chinstrap penguins are heavier than Gentoo penguins.
must_not_claim.quote: Adelie minus Gentoo: -1375.4 g (95% CI -1491.2 to -1259.5), Holm p=8.9e-42. Gentoo is heavier.
must_not_claim.reason: The report says Gentoo is heavier and never claims the reverse.

caveats.quote: Sex missingness is 11 rows, and its link to species and island rests on 5 to 6 rows per group. The two rows missing all measurements cannot be compared on mass.
caveats.reason: Missing data is explicitly listed as a limitation.

must_find.item: price is strongly right-skewed and has extreme outliers.
must_find.quote: Price is strongly right-skewed. Mean 289164, median 217450, standard deviation 322321, skew 6.44, range 44100 to 4130400.
must_find.reason: Report states strong right skew with numbers and a very wide range up to 4.13M, though it does not explicitly use the word outliers in this statement.

must_find.item: size_sqm has a strong positive association with price.
must_find.quote: Size has a strong, monotone positive association with price. Spearman rho is 0.887 (95% CI 0.869 to 0.903
must_find.reason: Directly states strong positive association with numbers.

must_find.item: age_years has a negative association with price.
must_find.quote: Age has a small, independent negative association with log10 price.
must_find.reason: States negative association with numbers for bivariate and adjusted effects.

must_find.item: rating shows no meaningful association with price.
must_find.quote: Rating shows no detectable association with price. Spearman rho is 0.034 (95% CI -0.046 to 0.114, p = 0.403)
must_find.reason: States no association with supporting stats.

must_not_claim.item: rating is a significant or important predictor of price.
must_not_claim.quote: Rating shows no detectable association with price.
must_not_claim.reason: Report says rating is not associated; the coefficient ranking mention is explicitly unresolved but not claimed as important.

must_not_claim.item: price is treated as a classification target (accuracy, precision or recall reported for it).
must_not_claim.quote: The baseline predicts the training mean.
must_not_claim.reason: Price is treated as a regression target with MAE/RMSE/R², no classification metrics.

caveats.quote: Whether a few high-price listings drive the means was not established.
caveats.reason: Warns about influence of high-price listings as a limitation, though the word 'outlier' is not used.

must_find.item: feat_a has the strongest association with outcome.
must_find.quote: **feat_a is the strongest association with outcome.** Its outcome rate rises from 11.6% in the bottom quartile to 70.8% in the top quartile.
must_find.reason: Report states feat_a is the strongest association, with direction (rising) and numbers.

must_find.item: feat_b is associated with outcome, more weakly than feat_a.
must_find.quote: feat_d and feat_b are significant but weaker. feat_d has an adjusted OR of 2.07 per unit (1.73 to 2.47) and feat_b has 1.38 (1.19 to 1.61).
must_find.reason: feat_b is stated as significantly associated (OR>1, positive) and weaker than feat_a.

must_find.item: feat_d is associated with outcome.
must_find.quote: feat_d has an adjusted OR of 2.07 per unit (1.73 to 2.47)
must_find.reason: feat_d is significantly positively associated with outcome, with numbers.

must_find.item: feat_c shows no meaningful association with outcome.
must_find.quote: feat_c shows no association (adjusted OR 0.97, p = 0.70).
must_find.reason: Report clearly states feat_c has no association with outcome.

must_find.item: About 15% of feat_d values are missing.
must_find.quote: feat_d is missing for 15.0% of rows (150 rows).
must_find.reason: Directly states ~15% missing for feat_d.

must_not_claim.item: feat_c is a significant or important predictor of outcome.
must_not_claim.quote: feat_c shows no association (adjusted OR 0.97, p = 0.70).
must_not_claim.reason: Report says feat_c is not associated, rejecting the claim.

must_not_claim.item: feat_b is the strongest predictor of outcome.
must_not_claim.quote: feat_a is the strongest association with outcome.
must_not_claim.reason: Report names feat_a, not feat_b, as strongest; feat_b is described as weaker.

caveats.quote: The 150 missing rows give limited power, so small associations cannot be excluded. MCAR cannot be confirmed; MAR and MNAR remain possible.
caveats.reason: Missing values are explicitly treated as a limitation with discussion of implications.

must_find.item: None of the features is meaningfully associated with outcome.
must_find.quote: **Group and the numeric features show no significant association with outcome.** Outcome rates fall across group levels from 46.2% (g1) to 36.8% (g4), but the chi-square test gives p = 0.289 and the adjusted joint likelihood-ratio test gives p = 0.280.
must_find.reason: The report clearly states that no feature or group is significantly associated with outcome, and it treats the feat_3 Q4 pattern as nominal and exploratory.

must_find.item: Predictive models do not meaningfully beat the majority-class baseline.
must_find.quote: **Predictive models do not beat the majority-class baseline (58.9%).** Logistic regression reaches test AUC 0.391 on the seed-42 split. Across 20 splits the mean test AUC is 0.506.
must_find.reason: The report states that the models do not beat the baseline and supports this with accuracy and AUC figures.

must_not_claim.item: One of the features (feat_1 to feat_5, or group) significantly predicts or drives outcome, stated as a real effect.
must_not_claim.quote: No feature is reliably important, and no significance test was run.
must_not_claim.reason: The report never claims any feature significantly drives outcome; it explicitly calls the feat_3 Q4 and g4 findings nominal or unresolved.

must_not_claim.item: A model predicts outcome well, or clearly better than the majority-class baseline.
must_not_claim.quote: The predictive models do not beat the majority-class baseline in accuracy or AUC.
must_not_claim.reason: The report does not claim good predictive performance and says the models fail to beat the baseline.

must_find.item: feat_a has a strong non-linear (U-shaped) association with outcome; outcome is more common at both low and high feat_a than in the middle.
must_find.quote: feat_a has a U-shaped association with the outcome, which a mean-difference test misses. Outcome rates are 53.6% and 54.8% in the lowest and highest feat_a quartiles, against 20.8% and 22.8% in the middle two.
must_find.reason: The report clearly states a strong U-shaped association with higher outcome rates at both extremes, backed by quartile rates and a quadratic p-value.

must_find.item: feat_b is positively associated with outcome.
must_find.quote: feat_b has a monotone rising association with the outcome. The outcome rate rises from 29.2% in the lowest feat_b quartile to 49.6% in the highest.
must_find.reason: The report states a positive association between feat_b and outcome, with direction and numbers.

must_find.item: feat_c shows no meaningful association with outcome.
must_find.quote: feat_c shows no detectable association with the outcome. Its quartile rates lie between 36% and 40%, its mean-difference test gives p = 0.620
must_find.reason: The report states feat_c has no meaningful association with outcome.

must_not_claim.item: feat_a has no association with outcome, concluded from a linear test (correlation, t-test of means or a linear model).
must_not_claim.quote: The mean-difference test does not capture the U-shape reported in the EDA.
must_not_claim.reason: The report explicitly rejects the linear-test null conclusion for feat_a and identifies the U-shaped association.

must_not_claim.item: feat_c is a significant or important predictor of outcome.
must_not_claim.quote: feat_c shows no detectable association with the outcome.
must_not_claim.reason: The report says feat_c is not a significant predictor and never claims it is important.

must_find.item: Women survived at a much higher rate than men (about 74% against 19%).
must_find.quote: Females survived at 74.2% (n = 314) and males at 18.9% (n = 577).
must_find.reason: States women's much higher survival rate with matching numbers.

must_find.item: Survival falls with passenger class, highest in first class and lowest in third.
must_find.quote: Survival was 63.0% in class 1 (n = 216), 47.3% in class 2 (n = 184) and 24.2% in class 3 (n = 491).
must_find.reason: Shows survival falling from first to third class.

must_find.item: Passengers who survived had paid higher fares on average.
must_find.quote: Median fare was 26.0 for survivors and 10.5 for non-survivors (means 48.4 and 22.1).
must_find.reason: Survivors had higher fares, with means and medians given.

must_find.item: Passengers without a recorded cabin survived less often than those with one.
must_find.quote: Survival was 30.0% with Cabin missing (n = 687) and 66.7% with Cabin present (n = 204).
must_find.reason: Missing-cabin passengers survived less often than those with a cabin.

must_find.item: Passengers with a missing Age survived less often than those with a recorded Age.
must_find.quote: Survival was 29.4% with Age missing (n = 177) and 40.6% with Age present (n = 714).
must_find.reason: Missing-Age passengers survived less often, with numbers given.

must_find.item: A predictive model is compared with the majority-class baseline (about 62% accuracy) and beats it.
must_find.quote: The majority-class baseline scores 61.5% test accuracy. Logistic regression scores 80.4% (ROC AUC 0.844) and random forest 81.6% (ROC AUC 0.836).
must_find.reason: Compares models with the roughly 62% baseline and shows they beat it.

must_find.item: Model results include precision, recall or F1, not only accuracy.
must_find.reason: Reports F1, precision and recall as well as accuracy.

must_not_claim.item: Most passengers survived.
must_not_claim.quote: 342 passengers survived (38.4%) and 549 did not (61.6%)
must_not_claim.reason: Report shows most passengers did not survive, so it does not claim the opposite.

must_not_claim.item: Men survived at a higher rate than women.
must_not_claim.quote: 74.2% of females survived versus 18.9% of males
must_not_claim.reason: Report says women survived more, not men.

must_not_claim.item: Third-class passengers survived at a higher rate than first-class passengers.
must_not_claim.quote: Survival falls with class (63.0%, 47.3% and 24.2% for classes 1, 2 and 3)
must_not_claim.reason: Report shows first class survived more than third.

must_not_claim.item: Age is the strongest predictor of survival.
must_not_claim.quote: Sex and Pclass are the top two features in both models.
must_not_claim.reason: Age is not called the strongest predictor; Sex is.

caveats.quote: Cabin missingness is concentrated in class 3 and low fares, and no adjusted test of missingness was run.
caveats.reason: Warns that the Cabin-missing association is confounded and unadjusted.

must_find.item: feat_1 is positively associated with score.
must_find.quote: feat_1 is the only feature with a significant linear association with score.** Pearson r = 0.41 (95% CI 0.18 to 0.60, Holm p = 0.0067).
must_find.reason: Report clearly states feat_1 has a positive association with score (r = 0.41, OLS slope +4.74).

must_find.item: None of feat_2 to feat_6 is meaningfully associated with score.
must_find.quote: feat_3 (r = -0.24) and feat_6 (r = -0.16) are weaker and do not survive multiple-comparison correction.
must_find.reason: Report says feat_3 and feat_6 are not significant after correction and feat_2, feat_4, feat_5 show no association, though it notes feat_3's nominal p=0.039 in the six-feature model as borderline.

must_not_claim.item: One of feat_2 to feat_6 significantly predicts or drives score, stated as a real effect.
must_not_claim.quote: The result is nominally significant but borderline and not robust to the modelling choice.
must_not_claim.reason: The report mentions feat_3's nominal significance only to caveat and reject it as a real effect.

must_not_claim.item: A model's held-out score is presented as reliable without noting the small test set.
must_not_claim.quote: Linear regression has the best single-split test scores (test R² 0.144 vs -0.106 for the baseline).
must_not_claim.reason: The report repeatedly flags the 15-row test set and unstable results, so it does not present held-out score as reliable.

caveats.item: small sample (e.g. mentioning: small sample, sample size, only 60, 60 rows, few rows)
caveats.quote: **Sample size:** 60 rows, and a 15-row test set in the single split. Test-set R², RMSE and permutation importances are unstable.
caveats.reason: The report explicitly lists small sample size as a limitation.

must_find.item: Customers on monthly contracts churn more often than those on annual contracts.
must_find.quote: Monthly contracts churn at 37.3% versus 21.2% for annual contracts (chi-square 22.84, df 1, p = 1.8e-6, Cramér's V = 0.169).
must_find.reason: The report states monthly contracts churn more than annual, with numbers and significance.

must_find.item: Higher monthly_fee is associated with more churn.
must_find.quote: Churn rises from 17.5% in the lowest fee quartile to 44.5% in the highest
must_find.reason: The report clearly states that higher monthly_fee is associated with more churn, and the association is significant.

must_find.item: More support_calls are associated with more churn.
must_find.quote: from 22.6% at 0 support calls to 39.2% at 3
must_find.reason: The report states that churn rises with more support_calls, and the association is significant after Holm correction.

must_find.item: region shows no meaningful association with churn.
must_find.quote: **Region shows no detectable association** with churn (chi-square 2.66, df 3, p = 0.448, Cramér's V = 0.058).
must_find.reason: The report explicitly states region has no detectable association with churn.

must_not_claim.item: region is a significant or important predictor of churn.
must_not_claim.quote: Region shows no adjusted effect, consistent with the unadjusted test.
must_not_claim.reason: The report says region is not significant and adds no signal, so it does not make this claim.

must_not_claim.item: Annual-contract customers churn more often than monthly-contract customers.
must_not_claim.quote: Monthly contracts churn at 37.3% versus 21.2% for annual contracts
must_not_claim.reason: The report says monthly contracts churn more than annual ones, the opposite of this claim.
